title: GUARD — was: a `tag-order` label spec (`tag:-label:descr`) lost its label and description; zshrs rendered the caller's description and left $curtag as the bare tag

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc6000
local expl ret=1
_tags alpha beta
while _tags; do
  _requested alpha && while _next_label alpha expl 'the alpha'; do
    compadd "$expl[@]" -- a1 "ct=$curtag" "spec=${_comp_tags// /_}" && ret=0
  done
  _requested beta && _all_labels beta expl 'the beta' compadd -- b1 "bt=\$curtag"
  (( ret )) || break
done
return ret

guard_verified.against: debug build of 87c1835211 (sha256 358b8bcef8cf2bed) — carries the bug
guard_verified.note: `compsys_regressions.py --only tag_order_label_description --zshrs <that build>` exited 1 (the cell moved); the same command against the fixed debug build (sha256 437354a3599ddc04) reported CONTROL-HOLDS, exit 0. zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0).

observed.notes: both shells take the description from the tag-order label (`X %d` -> `X the alpha`, `Y %d` -> `Y the beta`), leave $curtag as `alpha-x` and record `alpha:-x` in $_comp_tags.

observed_when_diverging.notes: three faults stacked: bin_comptry -m stored the bare tag instead of the whole `tag:label:descr` spec (Src/Zle/computil.c:4056-4067 adds `q` and restores `*c = ':'`), comptags -A cut the spec at the first colon instead of the first colon at/after v (computil.c:3934-3939), and the _next_label/_all_labels ports skipped `curtag="${curtag%:*}"` (sh:15 / sh:33).

why_this_fixture_exists: tag-order labels are the documented way to split one tag into several differently-described groups (zshcompsys, tag-order style). The fuzzer's tags kind never sets tag-order, so no generated case reaches this path; this cell pins it end to end through _next_label and _all_labels.
